creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Three separate bugs in one session had the same shape, and the shape cost more than any of the bugs did.

    a_2LMQSW9A8   a flake surfaced in whichever daemon-backed test lost the run, so it read as
                  a defect in whatever the reader was holding
    a_2LOHfLmsL   a write that landed reported "nothing about the session moved"
    a_2LONhlgwh   a container built around another worktree key failed at "Permission denied
                  (publickey)" rather than saying whose key it holds

Each is a different subsystem and each was found separately. What they share is that the failure hands the reader somebody else fault to investigate.

## What it cost

a_2LQZrPHbu has the tally: every slot in a four-agent round lost time to the first one, three of four first mistook it for their own work, and the integrator reported a red gate as green on top of it. None of that time went into the bug. It went into working out whose bug it was.

## The suggestion, which is a review question rather than a task

For an error path, "is this message accurate" is not enough - all three of these were accurate. The question that catches them is **does this name its cause, or does it describe the symptom and leave attribution to the reader?**

The DIS rule in the house style already asks for description, impact and solutions. This is the fourth thing, and it is the one that decides whether a reader starts warm or cold: say which component decided, and when the answer is "I do not know", say that rather than picking the nearest plausible actor.

Not obviously a task. It may be worth a line in AGENTS.md beside the DIS rule, or it may be worth nothing more than having been noticed. Filed because it recurred three times in one day and would otherwise be re-derived.
title: Ask of every error path: does this failure name its real cause?
